examples: The ancient tree is older than my grandpa.
We saw an ancient castle.
This ancient coin is very old.

more.def: From a time very long ago, often thousands of years in the past.
examples: We saw ancient tools in the museum that people used long ago.
Ancient people painted animals on the walls of caves.
The ancient city was buried under sand for centuries.

easy.def: A word that joins things together.
examples: I like milk and cookies.
Mom and Dad are here.
We ran and jumped.

more.def: A word used to join words, groups of words, or sentences, showing that they go together or that one thing comes after another.
examples: We packed sandwiches, apples, and juice for the hike.
The sun set, and the stars slowly came out.
He studied hard and passed the spelling test.

easy.def: One more, or a different one.
examples: I want another cookie.
Pick another card.
She has another dog.

more.def: One more of the same kind, or a different one.
examples: Can I have another glass of water, please?
This path is blocked, so let us try another way.
We will play another game after lunch.

easy.def: What you say or write when someone asks you.
examples: I know the answer.
Her answer was yes.
What is the answer?

more.def: What you say or write back to a question, or the solution to a problem.
examples: The answer to the riddle is a clock.
I checked my answers before I handed in the test.
She gave a quick answer to the teacher's question.

easy.def: To say something back when asked.
examples: I answer the phone.
He answered Mom.
Please answer me.

more.def: To speak or write in reply to a question, call, or letter.
examples: Please answer the phone if it rings.
She answered every question on the quiz.
He knocked on the door, but nobody answered.

easy.def: One or some, it does not matter which.
examples: Do you have any gum?
Pick any card.
I do not see any bugs.

more.def: Some, or one of a group when it does not matter which one.
examples: Do you have any questions about the story?
You can choose any book from the shelf.
We could not find any mud, so we went inside.
Is anybody home?
I do not see anybody.
Anybody can come.

more.def: Any person at all, no matter who.
examples: Anybody can learn to draw with enough practice.
Did anybody see where my hat went?
The pool is open to anybody who lives in town.
Can anyone help?
I do not see anyone.
Anyone can come.

more.def: Any person at all, no matter who.
examples: Anyone can learn to swim with enough practice.
Did anyone see my blue jacket?
The library is open to anyone who wants to read.
I will eat anything.
Do you see anything?
She can do anything.

more.def: Any thing at all, no matter which one.
examples: You can ask me anything about dinosaurs.
I could not find anything to eat in the cupboard.
He is brave and will try anything once.
It rained, but we went anyway.
I was scared, but I did it anyway.
She is small, but she won anyway.

more.def: In spite of something, or whatever else is true.
examples: It was raining, but we played outside anyway.
He was nervous but sang the song anyway.
The shirt was too big, but she wore it anyway.
